children: CBOT grain futures are lower in premarket, with most-active corn down 1%, soybeans off 0.6%, and wheat slipping 0.7%. For all three, the stronger U.S. dollar is creating pressure, says Argus in a note. "[They are] now coming to test important technical areas after a continuous decline observed since the beginning of the month," says the firm. A stronger dollar typically means that U.S. grain exports are less competitive on the world market versus other origins. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
